contexts.text: After death... the thought... becomes more instantaneous, and the... utterance of its singulars is consequently more prompt.
When Spirits are speaking together, they cannot utter one word of human language. Shown.
The books of the prophetic Enunciators in the Ancient Church. AC 2897.
The prophetical things (in the ancient Word) are called Enunciations - Enuntiata. AC 2898. AC 8273:4. AC 9942:5. CL 77:2. TCR 279.
Balaam gave forth an Enunciation. Quoted.

By every utterance of the mouth of Jehovah doth man live (; ) = in general, the Divine truth which proceeds from the Lord; thus all the truth of wisdom; in special, the Word, in which and from which are the things of wisdom. ( = the good and truth which proceed from Him. AC 5915:2.) AE 146:4. AE 730:36.
All the words (in the Word) involve spiritual things... and they are perceived in the Spiritual World from... the affection which results from the utterance of them. Explained.
(The Divine truth) thus becomes speech, which speech is uttered by the Spirits...
Utterance. Signified, Explained.
As mouth = voice, it = utterance... The mouth of man = the active or speaking thought, thus utterance.
Non-utterance. Signified, Explained.

By utterance, here, is not meant the utterance of the voice, that is, speech; for this utterance is natural; but by utterance is meant the confession of the Lord, and the preaching of faith in Him; for this utterance is spiritual.
That the things which he utters proceed from the Divine Human. Signified, Explained.

But to put in the mouth, when predicated of the Lord, = to proceed; for the Word which is uttered by a Spirit or Angel, proceeds from the Lord's Divine Human. For Aaron represents the doctrine of good and truth, which is uttered. Explained.
Hence it is that it is said that the things which are uttered, proceed from the Divine Human.

The form of truth Divine, that is, its perception, thought, and utterance, in the Third Heaven, so transcends that in the Second, that in the latter it cannot be apprehended... for it contains innumerable things which cannot be uttered in the Second Heaven... and the form of truth Divine in the Second Heaven in like manner transcends that in the First Heaven... Hence it is that the things which are uttered in those Heavens are such as no human mind has ever perceived, or ear heard.
Hence the things of the mouth, as the jaw?, lips, throat, tongue, = such things as belong to the utterance of truth.
The things written on those tables... were uttered before all the Israelitish people in a living voice by the Lord, (which) = immediate Divine inspiration in all the other things (of the Word) also.

It is impossible for the Angels to utter a single word of human language; it has been tried, but they could not; for they cannot utter anything but what is in complete accord with their affection. Explained.
Therefore the Enunciators say... (). The translators render it Composers of Proverbs; but they are to be called Enunciators, or Prophetic Enunciations. Explained.
When they want to utter Gods, and each as a Person by Himself, the endeavour to utter falls at once of itself into One God.
The Angels, in their own light, cannot compel themselves to utter [the word]. Gods. Explained.
For all utterances... from Heaven take place solely by means of ultimate things, such as are in the sense of the letter...
(A saying) which is uttered by every just man (from a law inscribed on the human heart).
I could not understand a whit, still less utter it.
More in a moment than could be uttered in an hour.
They could not utter (the words) one God. Explained.
To utter () = to inflow.
(These) organs serve the understanding for utterance and speech.
Although the things spoken are true as to the utterance, they are not true as to their understanding of them.
This word (of spiritual language) can indeed be uttered in natural language, but cannot be understood.
